nodes.description: INV-2: export orders nodes/edges/facets canonically and derived rows are content-addressed with a sentinel timestamp, so wipe+sync+export reproduces identical bytes

nodes.name: find surfaces each matched intent's grounding
nodes.description: loom find prints the file, locator and verdict of every implements edge under a matched intent, not just the node name — the edge a plain text search lacks

nodes.name: the next router serves the highest-priority asserted residue with a prompt contract
nodes.description: loom next returns failing, then stale, then uninspected asserted edges as a work item carrying allowed/forbidden actions and the evidence it expects

nodes.name: a symbol-pattern name is refused as an intent
nodes.description: INV-ATOM: functions/symbols are locators on implements edges, not intents; intent add rejects a symbol-shaped name unless --allow-symbol-name is given with a behavioral description

nodes.name: import loads every node before any edge
nodes.description: two-phase restore: parse-and-validate the whole export, then in one transaction insert all nodes before any edge, so an edge endpoint always resolves

nodes.name: maturity counts only leaf intents as needing grounding
nodes.description: an intent with hierarchy children is realized via its children; only leaves must ground to code, so a roll-up parent is not reported ungrounded

nodes.name: the verdict write boundary enforces the evidence, truth-class and lane gates
nodes.description: INV-4/5/6/7: record_verdict is the sole writer of asserted edge status; the verdict/show commands resolve the displayed 8-char id first, then it demands criterion+evidence for passing/failing, evidence for independent, refuses derived edges, and checks the agent's lane

nodes.name: changing a file re-opens the asserted edges grounded in it
nodes.description: content-hash ripple: sync stales the asserted edges depending on a changed codefile; an unchanged hash (or a first-ever observation) triggers no ripple, so there is no false churn

nodes.name: debt clusters are computed on read and never stored
nodes.description: INV-3: statistical signal (debt) is a projection derived from a snapshot; it is never written back as a node or edge

nodes.name: loom maintains a falsifiable graph for LLM-driven codebase work
nodes.description: durable, falsifiable memory an LLM drives: what the code should do, where it lives, how it is proven

nodes.name: iso5055-rel-resource-release
nodes.description: every acquired resource is released on all paths, including errors

detection_hints: in Rust, prefer RAII guards; a manual release missing on an early return is a leak

evidence_template.failing: src/<file>:<line> — resource not released on the error path
evidence_template.passing: src/<file>:<lines> — resources held by RAII guards, released on all paths

body.inspection_guide: 1. Find resource acquisition (files, locks, connections, handles). 2. Confirm release on all paths (RAII/Drop, defer, finally). 3. A leak on the error path is a violation.

nodes.name: no-panic-marker
nodes.description: production source should not panic at a boundary (unwrap/panic!)

nodes.name: iso5055-main-no-dead-or-duplicate-code
nodes.description: no unreachable or unused code; no copy-pasted logic where one definition belongs

detection_hints: red flag: the same logic copy-pasted in two places

evidence_template.passing: src/<file> — no dead code; shared logic factored

body.inspection_guide: 1. Look for unreachable/unused functions. 2. Look for duplicated logic across files. 3. Significant duplication or dead code is a violation.

nodes.name: max-file-size
nodes.description: a file should not exceed a maintainable line count

nodes.name: iso5055-rel-no-unchecked-failure
nodes.description: every fallible operation's failure path is handled or explicitly propagated

detection_hints: red flag: a Result discarded without handling

evidence_template.passing: src/<file>:<lines> — failures propagated via ? or handled explicitly

body.inspection_guide: 1. Find fallible calls (Result/Option, IO, parsing). 2. Confirm each failure is handled or propagated with `?`. 3. A swallowed error (unwrap_or_default on a real failure, ignored Result) is a violation.

nodes.name: complex-symbol
nodes.description: a function should stay below a cognitive complexity threshold

nodes.name: iso5055-sec-no-hardcoded-secrets
nodes.description: no credentials, tokens, or keys in source or committed config

detection_hints: grep: api_key, secret, password, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, token =
red flag: a long high-entropy string literal assigned to a secret-like name

evidence_template.passing: src/<file> — secrets read from env/secret store, none in source

body.inspection_guide: 1. Scan for literal secrets (API keys, passwords, private keys, connection strings). 2. Confirm secrets come from env or a secret store. 3. A literal credential in source is a violation.

nodes.name: iso5055-sec-no-injection
nodes.description: untrusted data is never concatenated into SQL/shell/HTML/query strings

detection_hints: red flag: user input interpolated into a query/command string

evidence_template.failing: src/<file>:<line> — untrusted input concatenated into a query

body.inspection_guide: 1. Find SQL/shell/HTML construction. 2. Confirm parameterization or escaping at the boundary. 3. String-concatenated untrusted input is a violation.
